title: cols-lab — 2- and 3-column layouts at every resolution

set.request: In our layout explorations, we need to thoroughly explore 2 and 3 column layouts, at all resolutions. the flex.auto system that breaks at a specified place might not work so well for 3440 2 and 3 columns.
steps: read the prior art (skill Q3, bento, decks, framework.css)
build the lab dir + cols.css word set
the indictment page - today's flex.auto measured
the matrix page - words x resolutions
measure all four widths headless, light + dark
count the hand-rolled 2-cols on the site
set.outcome:
**`.flex.auto` holds a ratio at 3440 and cannot stop, and its stack point is not a place.** The suspicion is half right — and the half that is right is the worse half. Six words shipped as a proposal-in-code, every ratio measured at 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440.

![the word set at 3440](/framework/ai/2026-08-30/cols-lab/shots/light-3440.png)

**The verdict, measured**

- **The ratio is fine.** `--grow: 2` reads exactly 2.000 at all four widths. The older per-child `--column` workaround decays 1.551 / 1.336 / **1.187** against an intended 2.000 — off 41% at 3440, and still shipping in `wire/specs.js`.
- **No ceiling — this is the 3440 failure.** A 32% aside measures **1010px** at 3440 with the ratio holding perfectly. `cols-main-aside` caps it at 416px and the main track takes the difference.
- **The place is not a place.** The threshold is `em`, and `em` here is a *viewport* clamp (14px -> 18px). The same **460px box** is two columns at a 400 viewport and a stack at 1920 and 3440 — same markup, same container, opposite layout. `cols-*` floors are `rem` and do not move.
- **Three tracks wrap 2 + 1** — an orphan at full width, measured at 400 and in the 460 box.
- **Where it is still right:** a wall of tiles, and two peers at 50/50 (exact 1.000 at every width).

**The word set** — `cols-half` `cols-golden` `cols-two-one` `cols-thirds` `cols-main-aside` `cols-rail-main-aside`. One rule: *the row, less the fixed tracks and one gap each, times this track's share of the weights*. A percentage basis (the decks finding), grow-by-weight so the slack cannot drift the ratio, a `rem` floor and an `em` rail, and `max(share, (floor - 100%) * 999)` instead of a container query — no wrapper element.

| word | 400 | 1280 | 1920 | 3440 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cols-half` | stacked | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| `cols-golden` | stacked | 1.618 | 1.618 | 1.618 |
| `cols-two-one` | stacked | 2.000 | 2.000 | 2.000 |
| `cols-thirds` | stacked | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| `cols-main-aside` | stacked | 2.125 | capped 416px | capped 416px |
| `cols-rail-main-aside` | stacked | 2.333 | capped 352px | capped 352px |

**Adoption** — 53 `flex auto` call sites and only ~8 are walls: ~26 are two-child rows, ~7 three-child. Plus 10 inline weighted `flex:` declarations, 26 two/three-track `grid-template-columns`, 49 `.basis` call sites. Recommended for `framework.css`: **`half`** and **`main-aside`** only, as `.cols.half` / `.cols.main-aside`. **No `framework.css` edit was made** — [the argument and the migration list](/framework/styles/layouts/cols/doc/adoption/).

**Open** — `golden`, `thirds`, `two-one` and `rail-main-aside` stay in the lab (thin usage evidence, argued in the note). The 10 inline `flex: "2 1 30em"` declarations should move to `--grow` regardless; that needs no new CSS and was left for the owner.
